inclusion_criteria: Primary sources (peer-reviewed papers, conference papers, arXiv preprints) with verifiable metadata (title, authors, year, venue/identifier).
Work that directly addresses NetOps, network configuration, configuration verification, or closely analogous structured-output operational domains (e.g., code synthesis, infra-as-code).
Papers describing datasets, simulators/emulators, validators, or benchmarks that are publicly accessible or documented with reproducible artifacts.
Research proposing or empirically evaluating mitigations (validation, constrained generation, tool-assisted correction, formal methods) for automated configuration or agentic workflows.
Recent work (2018–2026) prioritized for LLM/agentic methods; older foundational verification and SDN works included if directly relevant.
exclusion_criteria: Non-English sources unless they contain unique primary artifacts not available in English (document and justify if included).
News articles, unreferenced blog posts, or opinion pieces without primary artifacts or verifiable data, except when industry postmortems contain substantive technical details and are citable.
Papers unrelated to network operations or configuration-like structured-output tasks, unless they present methods of clear transferability (must be justified).
Proprietary or paywalled datasets/tools without sufficient documentation to verify claims (unless a peer-reviewed paper describes them with verifiable evaluation).
Work focused solely on generic language understanding benchmarks with no operational-action or structured-output component.
date_rationale: Prioritize 2018–2026 literature because advances in LLMs, agentic frameworks, and tool-augmented generation accelerated after 2018; include pre-2018 foundational work for formal verification, SDN, and program-synthesis methods when they are directly relevant to validators or theorem/constraint techniques.
